sections.content: How many people stayed in Sunderland after gaining qualifications?

Sunderland is a large town in the North East. Sunderland also has a university.

Sunderland has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Sunderland ended up with:

  • a similar number of graduates as it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 8,495 state-school pupils from Sunderland who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 2,190 (26%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 2,645 (31%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Sunderland to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Sunderland's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Sunderland in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Sunderland move to?

Of Sunderland's graduates, 485 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 80 of those graduates (16%) were living fairly locally, in the Sunderland travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Sunderland's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 315 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 115 of those qualified non-graduates (37%) were living fairly locally, in the Sunderland travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Sunderland's GCSE cohort:

  • 285 graduates left the North East
    • undefinedLondonundefinedundefined
  • 110 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the North East

In 2018 to 2019, 20% of graduates and 13% of qualified non-graduates living in Sunderland had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 2,080 graduates and 2,620 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Sunderland. This is compared with the 2,190 graduates and 2,645 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 80% of the graduates had also lived in Sunderland as GCSE pupils, while 20% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Sunderland in 2018 to 2019, 87% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 13% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
